title: Detect a Suspicious Transaction Pattern
real_world_story: A financial monitoring system records transaction types as a continuous sequence. Certain transaction patterns are known to be suspicious, and the system needs to identify every position where such a pattern occurs.

real_world_connection.system: Fraud detection and transaction monitoring system
real_world_connection.input_represents: A sequence of transaction codes and a suspicious transaction pattern
real_world_connection.target_represents: Every location where the suspicious pattern occurs
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: KMP pattern matching for efficiently locating repeated patterns in a transaction stream

problem_statement: Given a transaction sequence and a suspicious pattern, find every position where the pattern occurs in the sequence. Overlapping occurrences must also be reported.
task: Use KMP pattern matching to find all starting indices of the suspicious pattern.
input_format: The first line contains the transaction sequence as a string. The second line contains the suspicious pattern as a string.
output_format: Print all zero-based starting indices where the pattern occurs, separated by spaces. If the pattern does not occur, print -1.
constraints: Transaction sequence and pattern contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The suspicious pattern abc occurs starting at indices 2 and 7.
The pattern aaa occurs at indices 0, 1, and 2, including overlapping occurrences.

expected_algorithm.name: KMP Pattern Matching
expected_algorithm.reason: KMP avoids unnecessary character comparisons and efficiently finds every occurrence of a suspicious pattern in a large transaction stream.

complexity.where: N is the transaction sequence length and M is the pattern length.

hint: Build the LPS array for the suspicious pattern.
Scan the transaction sequence using the KMP matching process.
When the complete pattern is found, record its starting index.
After finding a match, continue using the LPS array to detect overlapping matches.
real_world_takeaway: Efficient pattern matching allows fraud-monitoring systems to detect suspicious sequences quickly even when transaction streams become very large.
